document_title: Pitched as data centers. Passed as an inquiry.
post_copy:
"Seems high" is how AIDEA's January minutes record board member Andrew Guy's view of $20 million for Alaska Data Corporation.

He asked to see a budget. Resolution G26-03 had arrived with the amount blank. A motion wrote in $20 million and it passed unanimously, one commissioner absent.

On November 9th Gov. Dunleavy pitched the company for distributed data centers and paired it with InvestNorth, a platform for tokenized stakes. The resolution is titled an inquiry. Its text never says data center. The January discussion did. No offering was available at launch.

Inside are the blank and the vote, $20 million against AIDEA's $1.7 billion balance sheet and $10 million yearly budget Brefczynski cited, and what the launch left out.

Would you buy an InvestNorth stake before reading the feasibility finding the resolution puts first?

#AIDEA #AlaskaDataCenters #Tokenization

slides.body: Gov. Dunleavy launched Alaska Data Corporation, an AIDEA subsidiary meant to facilitate distributed data centers, and InvestNorth, a state-sponsored platform for tokenized stakes, some possibly reserved for Alaska residents.
The resolution reached the board with the amount left blank. Board member Albert Fogle amended his motion to insert $20 million, as staff recommended.

slides.headline:
"seems
high"
slides.body: That is how the minutes record board member Andrew Guy's view of the amount. He asked to see a budget for the funds. The resolution then passed unanimously, with one commissioner absent.

slides.kicker: AS STATED TO THE BOARD · JANUARY 21ST
slides.headline:
Small for the balance sheet.
Two years of the budget.
slides.body: Brefczynski told the board AIDEA has a $1.7 billion balance sheet and a $10 million annual operating budget. He described the $20 million as multi-year capital, with no intent to return for more.

slides.headline:
"distributed
data
centers"
slides.body: The text of the resolution never says data center. The January discussion did.

slides.headline:
"No investment
offering"
slides.body: No specific projects. No construction schedules. No investment amounts. No job totals. No terms for AIDEA's capital.

slides.headline: Four weeks.
slides.body: The next administration inherits a company capitalized with $20 million and a platform with no offering. The company's president, Brandon Brefczynski, presented the resolution in January as AIDEA's deputy director.

slides.headline:
The resolution says
feasible first.
slides.body: Section 7 lets the platform proceed only after the inquiry finds it feasible and in the public interest, and AIDEA's chief financial officer approves.

editor_notes_for_email: The caption ships byte for byte from caption.txt (880 characters, hook 125). Applied at scoring: "distributed data centers" is paraphrased without quote marks in the caption and slide 06 carries the kicker AS REPORTED, because the phrase is how Must Read Alaska and Crypto Briefing word the announcement and not a verified quote of the governor. C50, the noon December 7th inauguration, now cites the Alaska Constitution, Article III, Section 4, and the first comment no longer carries the Alaska Public Media URL whose slug named a candidate as leading. "Its text never says data center" stands on a full read and a grep of the resolution and staff memo (zero hits), with the caveat that the check ran on OCR text. No primary source was found for the November 9th announcement, so C01 and C15 rest on Must Read Alaska and Crypto Briefing; investnorth.com showed only a title. Only the lead story survived the claims gate; the Enstar gas exchange and the Waymo Fairbanks testing leads were killed under the single-source rule. No winner of the governor's race is named or implied anywhere.
